newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: PLO seeks U.N. council meeting on Israeli building.
newsitem.headline: PLO seeks U.N. council meeting on Israeli building.

text.p: The Palestine Liberation Organisation called on Tuesday for an immediate meeting of the Security Council to adopt a resolution demanding a halt to a controversial Israeli building project in Arab East Jerusalem.

In identical letters to both the council president and Secretary-General Kofi Annan, the PLO's U.N. observer, Nasser al-Kidwa, said Israel had "begun the actual work for construction of a new settlement in the Jabal Abu Ghneim area to the south of occupied East Jerusalem."

"The Israeli occupying authorities closed off the area, declaring it a military zone, and sent in bulldozers to start the work," he said, referring to plans to build 6,500 homes for Jews on a hill between Jerusalem and Bethlehem, called Har Homa by Israel, which captured it during the 1967 Middle East War.

"We call upon the Security Council to convene an immediate, official meeting to consider this serious situation, and to adopt a resolution in this regard, clearly demanding the immediate and full cessation of all settlement activities in Jabal Abu Ghneim, East Jerusalem and throughout the occupied Palestinian territory.
"We believe that it is the duty of the council to act and to act rapidly in response to such grave developments," he added.
The request is likely to be considered during council consultations on Wednesday.

The 185-member General Assembly adopted a resolution by an overwhelming majority last Thursday calling on Israel to refrain from all actions or measures, including settlement activities, which alter the facts on the ground.
This followed the vetoing by the United States March 7 of a similar resolution in the Security Council.

Although the United States, like virtually all other speakers in both the Assembly and council debates, criticised Israel's decision to build the planned neighbourhood, it said the United Nations was not the appropriate forum for dealing with issues that should be settled bilaterally between Israel and the Palestinians.

Earlier Tuesday, a U.N. spokesman said the secretary-general had "learned with disappointment and deep concern that, despite international appeals, the Israeli authorities" had decided to proceed with the construction work.
"He calls on the parties to do their utmost to find mutually acceptable solutions and proceed with the peace negotiations," the statement added.
